groups.name: owner_identity_and_registry
groups.base_provenance: The same owner-relative object is initialized, registered as tag 0x73, published to global 0x3326AE0, updated, and passed to teardown. Adjacent owner object begins at +0x7FF1A0.

groups.name: network_index_write
groups.base_provenance: Global object in R14; lookup by peer ID in known network owner supplies network index. Index is multiplied by 24 with no local <4 bound, then writes peer ID, integer accumulators, and a flag.

groups.name: consume_then_clear_snapshot
groups.base_provenance: Input object becomes R14. Rebuild final records by active object ordinal, resolve corresponding peer ID and network index, copy 24 bytes from index cache after checking peer ID, then clear exactly 0x60 bytes of the cache.

groups.name: adjacent_live_typed_storage
groups.base_provenance: RIP global provenance at reset; the region at +C500 is cleared independently, then has its own entry keys, integer/float/bool values, and type discriminator consumed by the direct serializer 0x62DF40.

groups.name: object_append_four_bounds
groups.base_provenance: Three independent code entries append corresponding objects into this global subsystem. Each checks total count+1 <=4 and explicitly writes to address zero on failure. Direct execution dispatch for these entries is not yet identified.

groups.name: move_and_compact_parallel_records
groups.base_provenance: 0x631930 and inlined 0x631CE0 move both pointer records and complete 40-byte records, update the embedded lookup map, and use three lifecycle counts. Owner update also calls 0x631930.

groups.name: final_snapshot_fixed_four_consumers
groups.base_provenance: The same global object feeds a four-record peer-ID search at +C440 and a fully unrolled four-term sum of record+0xC fields. Exact high-level system / resource names are not proven by these instructions.

limits: No live process access; no fifth player, object insertion, eight-player match, or playable mod verified.
Index>=4 crosses the proven four-record member-array boundary, not necessarily the heap allocation boundary.
The constructor embeds its own map storage and registers the object pointer; changing only the published global cannot relocate all references.
Scalar integer accumulator count is data-driven; this evidence does not identify its resource names or bound it to three.
Final snapshot ordinal, subsystem registered-object ordinal, and network index are distinct addressing paths; equality is not asserted.
The three add functions are identified implementations; their actual runtime dispatch remains unresolved.
Field scans identify encoded displacement candidates and do not exhaust computed or uncaptured references.
